quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers to dangers or special situations ahead.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use half a lane.
Pass the motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles with the same road rights as other vehicles. Give them a full lane width so they have room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. Always slow down at railroad crossings. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must yield to them.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you need to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to a dangerous situation.

questions.question: Which describes a defensive driver?
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers watch for danger and prepare to respond. They stay alert to everything happening around them.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights or a siren.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest thing to do is:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go much faster or slower than other traffic. Drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the speed limit.

questions.question: In foggy weather, you should:

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive no faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights when you can see less than 500 feet ahead. Do not use high beams in fog because the light will bounce back and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down but keep driving in your lane.
Move to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, pull to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: To make a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
On the left side of the street.
On the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move as far right as possible before turning right. Do not cross other lanes to make your turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time. Which vehicle must yield?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same as:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Then yield to all traffic that does not have to stop before you proceed.

questions.question: Night driving compared to day driving is:
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as well in the dark. Other vehicles' headlights can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers may be on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers that left turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach carefully and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for an approaching train.
Only proceed when a flagger clears you to do so, if one is present.

questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with caution. Check both directions for trains before crossing. Listen for approaching trains. Follow a flagger's instructions if one is present.

questions.question: To turn left from a multi-lane, one-way street or highway, start from:
questions.explanation: When turning left from a multi-lane street or highway, start from the left lane.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangle signs tell drivers to:
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangle signs mean you should yield. Only proceed when the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians, and it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are separated by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop your vehicle to keep them safe.

questions.question: What should you do to prepare for dangers ahead on the road?

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides of it.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides of it.
questions.explanation: Look for problems before you reach them. Check the entire road ahead and the sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: What do larger vehicles have?

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do when another driver is trying to pass your car?

options.text: Signal to them when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to allow safe passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to allow safe passing.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help the passing vehicle return to the right lane safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. Do not make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Gently brake and slowly steer back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and slowly steer back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep them off the pavement and gently slow down using the brakes. When you reach a safe speed, turn the wheel to return to the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: What must you do if a bus is signaling to re-enter the road after a stop?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to return to the road after stopping to pick up or drop off passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus enter traffic safely.

questions.question: How far ahead should you look to avoid sudden braking or turns?
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle to avoid sudden braking or sharp turns. This gives drivers behind you time to react to your movements.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When conditions are less than perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when the road is wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when any conditions are not perfect. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions even if you are at the speed limit.

questions.question: What should a driver do when entering an interstate from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Assume that other drivers will move to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from a ramp, yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you find an opening in traffic.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way intersection with stop signs. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way intersection, if two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You must wait until they pass, then you may go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must give the right-of-way to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked car and the owner is not there. What should you do?

options.text: You must wait for police to arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and details of what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and details of what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit an unattended parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive the same as you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your vehicle needs more time to stop in these conditions.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: Traffic is backing up behind you because you are driving slowly. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let the other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic around you is unsafe. On a two-lane road, you must pull over and let cars behind you pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and check if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: You hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Make a clear path for the emergency vehicle. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly to the side as soon as you can.

questions.question: How can you make sure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving?

options.text: Stay in good physical shape and have regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limits and only drive when you can do so safely.
